questions.q: Explain how energy flows and matter cycles in the Earth system.
answer: The Earth is a system of interacting spheres — the land, water, air and the biosphere of living things — through which energy flows and matter cycles.

answer.text: Energy comes mainly from the Sun and flows in one direction: green plants, the producers, capture it, and it passes to consumers and then to decomposers. Only about ten per cent of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next, which is why food chains are short.

Unlike energy, matter is recycled through biogeochemical cycles. The water cycle moves water through evaporation and rain, the carbon cycle balances photosynthesis and respiration, the nitrogen cycle passes nitrogen from air to plants and back, and the oxygen cycle links photosynthesis and respiration. These cycles keep the Earth system in balance.

questions.q: What is the ozone layer, and how are human activities threatening the Earth system?

answer.text: The ozone layer is a region of ozone gas high in the stratosphere that shields living things by absorbing the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays. Certain man-made chemicals called CFCs damage this layer, creating the ozone hole and letting through more harmful radiation.

Human activities are disturbing the balance of the Earth system in many ways. Pollution fouls the air, water and soil; the burning of fossil fuels increases greenhouse gases and causes global warming and climate change; and deforestation and over-exploitation cause a loss of biodiversity.
To keep the Earth system healthy, resources must be used sustainably, pollution reduced, and forests and wildlife conserved.
